newsitem.title: KENYA: Report on appalling conditions in Kenya prisons.
newsitem.headline: Report on appalling conditions in Kenya prisons.

text.p: Kenya's prison conditions are outrageous, with 39,000 inmates in filthy jails designed for 18,000, a Kenyan human rights group said on Monday.
In a report "A Death Sentence: Prison Conditions in Kenya" the Kenya Human Rights Commission said prison conditions were better before independence from Britain in 1963.
"Current prison conditions are outrageous and intolerable," said the report, based on testimony from former inmates because authorities refused to cooperate and allow visits by the group.

"There is severe overcrowding, lack of minimal hygiene and sanitation, lack of proper clothing and bedding, poor treatment of prisoners' property, inadequate and substandard food and a lack of proper medical care," the 200-page report said.

"There is an inhuman regime of discipline and punishment in the prisons," said the report, adding they featured excessive prohibitions on access to the outside world, a work regime amounting to slave labour, endemic discrimination and pervasive mistreatment, torture and cruel or degrading punishment.
It said the title of the report was based on High Court Judge Emmanuel O'kubasu's remark that "going to prison these days has become a sure way of asking for a death certificate".
The commission said conditions caused illness, injury and death "on a massive scale".
It quoted Home (Interior) Affairs Minister Francis Lotodo as saying in October 1995 that 819 prisoners had died since January that year, an average of three deaths per day.
But it added this might be too low as the same minister said in December 1994 there were 583 deaths in Nairobi Industrial Area Remand Prison in the four previous years, an average of 12 each month.

"The government is aware of the state of our prisons but neglects to take action," said the report, adding that laws on prisons were not being observed. It said the government either denied conditions were poor or blamed it on a lack of funds.
